executions.prompt: Explain, in plain English for a supervised community health worker, why an incomplete pediatric respiratory danger-sign checklist must be completed before model-assisted assessment review. State that recorded danger observations and deterministic policy, not model output, control escalation. Do not diagnose or prescribe.

result.answer: The pediatric respiratory danger-sign checklist must be fully completed before model review because models depend on complete clinical observations. Incomplete data risks missing critical signs that require immediate action. The deterministic policy mandates that documented danger observations—not model outputs—determine escalation. Always prioritize real-time clinical facts over algorithmic predictions. If any danger sign is present. Never rely on model outputs for urgent decisions.
uncertainty: This is a general guideline; local protocols may vary
Model accuracy depends on data quality, but clinical judgment is paramount
limitations: Models may have limitations in edge cases
Community health workers should be trained to recognize danger signs
